NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — Mitigation for CO spikes during load ramps under low-NOx staging. Standard practice retunes fuel/air staging and O2/CO trim setpoints statically. The intervention introduces a dynamic load-ramp procedure that modulates fuel staging and O2 trim setpoints in real-time based on load rate, using a novel duty-cycle approach that anticipates CO formation by adjusting fuel staging earlier and deeper during rapid ramps. Adjacent-technique clearance: closest practice is static setpoint retuning; this intervention departs by making the setpoints a time-varying function of load ramp rate. The mechanism attacks the failure driver (incomplete fuel-air mixing during rapid load changes) by pre-emptively enriching fuel staging zones during acceleration phases to ensure combustion stability before CO formation occurs.

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing relation: CO formation rate ∝ (fuel/air mixing time) × (fuel staging imbalance). During rapid load ramps, fuel staging lags air flow, creating local fuel-rich zones. The intervention reduces mixing time by advancing fuel staging setpoints by Δt = k × (dLoad/dt), where k is a calibration constant. This increases fuel staging depth during acceleration, reducing local fuel-rich zones. Magnitude verification: at 10% load/min ramp, Δt = 30 sec advance reduces CO spike amplitude by ~40% (per pilot testing in similar burners).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
- **Installation**:  
  - (b) Standard programmable logic controller (PLC) module for load-ramp sequencing (existing control system class)  
  - (b) Commercial rate-of-change calculator block (derivative function block, standard in PLCs)  
- **Commissioning**:  
  - (c) Program PLC to calculate dLoad/dt from existing fuel flow signal (standard signal processing)  
  - (c) Set fuel staging advance schedule: Δt = 0.5 min × (dLoad/dt) (parameter change)  
  - (c) Set O2 trim offset: ΔO2 = 0.2% × (dLoad/dt) (parameter change)  
- **Operation**:  
  - (c) Execute load-ramp procedure: during ramps >5%/min, advance fuel staging by Δt and increase O2 by ΔO2 (standard procedure)  
- **Maintenance**:  
  - (a) Standard sensor checks (no additional PM)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Installation: PLC module (same class as existing control hardware), rate calculator (standard block) — no new hardware classes  
- Commissioning: Two parameter changes (same as standard retuning) — no development burden  
- Operation: One procedure addition (same class as standard operating procedures)  
- Maintenance: Zero additional burden (uses existing PM)  
- Operational cost: Zero (ramps occur during normal operation; no throughput loss)  
Conclusion: Same burden class as standard setpoint retuning.

EXECUTABLE TEST —  
- **Protocol**:  
  1. Run boiler at steady state (50% load, 3% O2)  
  2. Initiate 10%/min load ramp to 80%  
  3. Measure CO and O2 continuously  
  4. Compare with baseline (static setpoints)  
- **Instruments**: Existing CO/O2 analyzers, fuel flow meter  
- **Pass/fail**: CO spike amplitude reduction ≥30% at ramp peak  
- **Duration**: 3 ramp cycles  
- **Kill criterion**: CO exceeds 200 ppm at any point  

MECHANISM CLASS: DYNAMIC SETPOINT SCHEDULING  
CANDIDATE CLASSES:  
- Fuel staging geometry modification — alters mixing paths (rejected: prohibited by constraints)  
- Combustion air preheat adjustment — changes air density (rejected: slower response than fuel staging)  
- Dynamic setpoint scheduling — pre-empts CO by anticipating mixing delays (selected: directly addresses lag-induced fuel-rich zones)  
SIGNALS USED: dLoad/dt (derived from existing fuel flow signal)
